title: World Cup Day 3: Qatar and Switzerland drew 1-1; Brazil and Morocco drew 1-1
excerpt: Group stage action from New York/New Jersey, San Francisco Bay Area on June 13 — 2 matches, no shortage of drama.
body:
Day 3 of the 2026 FIFA World Cup delivered 2 matches and 4 goals on Saturday, June 13. The tournament, spread across the United States, Canada, and Mexico, continued its group stage with action that will resonate in standings tables and living rooms alike — not least in the Indian-American households tuning in from cities that are, for once, hosting the spectacle rather than streaming it from half a world away.

Here is everything you need to know.

## Qatar 1-1 Switzerland
*Group B · Levi's Stadium, San Francisco Bay Area*

A 1-1 draw was probably a fair reflection of a tightly contested match between Qatar and Switzerland at Levi's Stadium. Both teams created chances, both teams scored, and both teams will look at moments where they might have won it. In the end, a share of the spoils was the just outcome.

For both sides, the arithmetic is clear: a point is better than none, but wins are the currency of a group stage. Their remaining Group B fixtures take on added importance.


![World Cup — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/fb/Kitzbuehel_slalom_ganslernhang_2010.jpg)



> **"South Asian fans dotted the stands, many attending their first-ever World Cup match on home soil."**



Levi's Stadium in the Bay Area — home to one of the largest Indian-American populations in the country — provided the backdrop. South Asian fans dotted the stands, many attending their first-ever World Cup match on home soil.

## Brazil 1-1 Morocco
*Group C · MetLife Stadium, New York/New Jersey*

A 1-1 draw was probably a fair reflection of a tightly contested match between Brazil and Morocco at MetLife Stadium. Both teams created chances, both teams scored, and both teams will look at moments where they might have won it. In the end, a share of the spoils was the just outcome.

For both sides, the arithmetic is clear: a point is better than none, but wins are the currency of a group stage. Their remaining Group C fixtures take on added importance.

The match was played at MetLife Stadium in the heart of NJ/NY's massive desi community. Indian-American fans made their presence felt in the stands — the tri-state area is home to one of the densest concentrations of South Asian Americans in the country.


![San Francisco Bay Area — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/OAKLAND%2C_CA%2C_USA_-_Skyline_and_Bridge.JPG/3840px-OAKLAND%2C_CA%2C_USA_-_Skyline_and_Bridge.JPG)


## What It Means for the Standings

In Group B, **Qatar** and **Switzerland** each take a point — not the worst outcome, but not the result either side wanted. In Group C, **Brazil** and **Morocco** each take a point — not the worst outcome, but not the result either side wanted. 

With 48 teams and a format that sends the top two from each group — plus the eight best third-placed sides — into the round of 32, the margins are tighter than they appear. Goal difference could prove decisive.

## What's Next

Day 4 (Sunday, June 14) brings 5 more group stage matches:

- **Australia vs Turkey** — Group D at BC Place, Vancouver
- **Germany vs Curaçao** — Group E at NRG Stadium, Houston
- **Netherlands vs Japan** — Group F at AT&T Stadium, Dallas
- **Ivory Coast vs Ecuador** — Group E at Lincoln Financial Field, Philadelphia
- **Sweden vs Tunisia** — Group F at Estadio BBVA, Monterrey
